cards.text: This song is from David, for the choirmaster, with stringed instruments. The note at the top tells us the moment: the Ziphites went to Saul, king of Israel, and said, “Is David not hiding among us?” Saul was out to take David's life (1 Samuel 23:15).
Think about that, friend. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer and NOBODY came looking for me, but David can't even hide without the neighbors handing out DIRECTIONS!

cards.question: David's hiding, and the Ziphites are tipping off Saul. What does David do first in this song?

answers.text: He asks God to save him
He runs for the next town

cards.question: In the next line, David asks God to send him a sign.
David begs God to hear his prayer and listen to the words of his mouth. Why is he pleading like this?

answers.text: Ruthless men are out to take his life
His own family has turned against him
He has fallen sick and can't get up

cards.question: David says the ruthless men rising up against him have no regard for ___.

cards.text: Then comes the word Selah. And right after it, this song turns a corner.

cards.question: After the Selah, David says God has left him to face these ruthless men alone.

cards.text: Ruthless men are after his life, and David says, “Surely God is my helper.” That's like the power going out and somebody calmly saying, “Relax, I know who's got the flashlight.”

cards.question: God is David's helper. What else does David call the Lord in that same line?

cards.text: Now David turns to his enemies, and to who's going to deal with them.

cards.question: David says he'll pay his enemies back himself.

cards.text: David says of God, “He will reward my enemies with evil.” Then he prays, “In Your faithfulness, destroy them.”
Then David stops talking about his enemies and makes God a promise.

cards.question: David's enemies are still out there. What does he promise to do for the LORD?

answers.text: Sacrifice freely and praise His name
Build Him a house of cedar
Fast and pray for forty days

cards.question: Back at the start, David asked God to save him by His name. Now David says he'll praise the LORD's name because it is good.
David closes his song by giving the reason for his praise. What does he say God has done for him?

answers.text: Made him king over all Israel
Given him a city of his own

cards.question: In the last line, David says his eyes have looked in ___ on his foes.

cards.text: Look at that, friend. I had some rough days in that drawer and never wrote ONE song, but David gets his hiding spot given away and writes one for the CHOIR!

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 9 quotes "Surely God is my helper.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The Ziphites appear for the first time here, but the card never says who they are. Saul is introduced as king of Israel, but the Ziphites are not.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card says "Saul was out to take David's life (1 Samuel 23:15)." That gives away the answer to card 5, which asks why David is pleading. The right answer there is "Ruthless men are out to take his life."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card states a fact from 1 Samuel 23:15 and cites it in the text. The card's verses field lists only Psalm 54:1. A range written like Psalm 54:1-1 Samuel 23:15 can't express both.
findings.question: When a story card uses a fact from outside the passage, should that verse go in the card's verses field? If so, in what format, since the citation rule describes a single range from the first verse used to the last?

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke and tells no part of the passage. It still cites Psalm 54:1.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess what "the next line" says before any card has told verse 2. The baker has nothing to reason from, so a pick is luck. Verse 2 is only told afterward, in card 5's question.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The card asks what else David calls the Lord in the same line, with answers "sustainer of his soul," "shield around his house" and "keeper of his crown." This tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out, like the bad anointing-oil example for Psalm 23.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question says "David's enemies are still out there." The text never says this. Verse 7 says God "has delivered me from every trouble" and David's eyes "have looked in triumph on my foes," so the added detail goes against the text.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The last story card is only a joke that looks back at the superscription. It tells no part of the passage and works as a recap. It still cites Psalm 54:7.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
